[Section titled: How can Exchange Online customers use Outbound SMTP DANE with DNSSEC?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#how-can-exchange-online-customers-use-outbound-smtp-dane-with-dnssec) ## How can Exchange Online customers use Outbound SMTP DANE with DNSSEC? As an Exchange Online customer, you don't need to do anything to configure this enhanced email security for your outbound email. We built this enhanced email security for you, and it's ON by default for all Exchange Online customers. Exchange Online uses this security when the destination domain advertises support for DANE. To reap the benefits of sending email with DNSSEC and DANE checks, communicate to your business partners with whom you exchange email that they need to implement DNSSEC and DANE so they can receive email using these standards. [Section titled: Troubleshooting sending emails with SMTP DANE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#troubleshooting-sending-emails-with-smtp-dane) ## Troubleshooting sending emails with SMTP DANE Currently, there are four error codes for DANE when sending emails with Exchange Online. Microsoft is actively updating this error code list. You can see the errors in: 1. The Exchange Admin Center portal through the Message Trace Details view. 2. NDRs generated when a message isn't sent due to a DANE or DNSSEC failure. 3. Remote Connectivity Analyzer tool [Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer](https://testconnectivity.microsoft.com/tests/o365). Expand table | NDR Code | Description | | --- | --- | | 4/5.7.321 | starttls-not-supported: Destination mail server must support TLS to receive mail. | | 4/5.7.322 | certificate-expired: Destination mail server's certificate is expired. | | 4/5.7.323 | tlsa-invalid: The domain failed DANE validation. | | 4/5.7.324 | dnssec-invalid: Destination domain returned invalid DNSSEC records. | Note Currently, when a domain signals that it supports DNSSEC but fails DNSSEC checks, Exchange Online doesn't generate the 4/5.7.324 dnssec-invalid error. It generates a generic DNS error: `4/5.4.312 DNS query failed` We're actively working to remedy this known limitation. If you receive this error statement, navigate to the Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer and perform the DANE validation test against the domain that generated the 4/5.4.312 error. The results show if it's a DNSSEC issue or a different DNS issue. [Section titled: Troubleshooting 4/5.7.321 starttls-not-supported](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#troubleshooting-457321-starttls-not-supported) ### Troubleshooting 4/5.7.321 starttls-not-supported This error usually indicates an issue with the destination mail server. After receiving the message: 1. Check that you entered the destination email address correctly. 2. Alert the destination email administrator that you received this error code so they can determine if the destination server is configured correctly to receive messages using TLS. 3. Retry sending the email and review the Message Trace Details for the message in the Exchange Admin Center portal. [Section titled: Troubleshooting 4/5.7.322 certificate-expired](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#troubleshooting-457322-certificate-expired) ### Troubleshooting 4/5.7.322 certificate-expired The sending email server must present a valid X.509 certificate that isn't expired. X.509 certificates must be renewed after their expiration, commonly annually. After receiving the message: 1. Alert the destination email administrator that you received this error code and provide the error code string. 2. Allow time for the destination server certificate to be renewed and the TLSA record to be updated to reference the new certificate. Then, retry sending the email and review the Message Trace Details for the message in the Exchange Admin Center portal. [Section titled: Troubleshooting 4/5.7.323 tlsa-invalid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#troubleshooting-457323-tlsa-invalid) ### Troubleshooting 4/5.7.323 tlsa-invalid This error code relates to a TLSA record misconfiguration and can only be generated after a DNSSEC-authentic TLSA record is returned. Many scenarios during the DANE validation occur after the record is returned that can result in the code being generated. Microsoft is actively working on the scenarios that this error code covers, so that each scenario has a specific code. Currently, one or more of these scenarios could cause the generation of the error code: 1. The destination mail server's certificate doesn't match with what the authentic TLSA record expects. 2. The authentic TLSA record is misconfigured. 3. The destination domain is under attack. 4. Any other DANE failure. After receiving the message: 1. Alert the destination email administrator that you received this error code and provide them with the error code string. 2. Allow time for the destination email admin to review their DANE configuration and email server certificate validity. Then, retry sending the email and review the Message Trace Details for the message in the Exchange Admin Center portal. [Section titled: Troubleshooting 4/5.7.324 dnssec-invalid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#troubleshooting-457324-dnssec-invalid) ### Troubleshooting 4/5.7.324 dnssec-invalid Exchange Online generates this error code when the destination domain indicates it's DNSSEC-authentic but Exchange Online can't verify it as DNSSEC-authentic. After receiving the message: 1. Alert the destination email administrator that you received this error code and provide them with the error code string. 2. Allow time for the destination email admin to review their domain's DNSSEC configuration. Then, retry sending the email and review the Message Trace Details for the message in the Exchange Admin Center portal. [Section titled: Troubleshooting receiving emails with SMTP DANE](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#troubleshooting-receiving-emails-with-smtp-dane) ## Troubleshooting receiving emails with SMTP DANE Currently, admins of receiving domains can use two methods to validate and troubleshoot their DNSSEC and DANE configuration to receive email from Exchange Online by using the following standards: 1. Adopt SMTP TLS-RPT (Transport Layer Security Reporting) introduced in [RFC8460](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8460) 2. Use the Remote Connectivity Analyzer tool [Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer](https://testconnectivity.microsoft.com/tests/o365) TLS-RPT [https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8460](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8460) is a reporting mechanism for senders to provide details to destination domain administrators about DANE and MTA-STS successes and failures with those respective destination domains. To receive TLS-RPT reports, you only need to add a TXT record in your domain's DNS records that includes the email address or URI you want the reports to be sent to. Exchange Online sends TLS-RPT reports in JSON format. The following table shows an example of a record: | Type | Domain Name | TTL | Record | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TXT | \_smtp.\_tls.microsoft.com | 3600 | v=TLSRPTv1;rua=https://tlsrpt.azurewebsites.net/report | The second method is to use the Remote Connectivity Analyzer [Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer](https://testconnectivity.microsoft.com/tests/o365), which can do the same DNSSEC and DANE checks against your DNS configuration that Exchange Online does when sending email outside the service. This method is the most direct way of troubleshooting errors in your configuration to receive email from Exchange Online by using these standards. When troubleshooting errors, the following error codes might be generated: | NDR Code | Description | | --- | --- | | 4/5.7.321 | starttls-not-supported: Destination mail server must support TLS to receive mail. | | 4/5.7.322 | certificate-expired: Destination mail server's certificate has expired. | | 4/5.7.323 | tlsa-invalid: The domain failed DANE validation. | | 4/5.7.324 | dnssec-invalid: Destination domain returned invalid DNSSEC records. | Note Currently, when a domain signals that it supports DNSSEC but fails DNSSEC checks, Exchange Online doesn't generate the 4/5.7.324 dnssec-invalid error. It generates a generic DNS error: `4/5.4.312 DNS query failed` We're actively working to remedy this known limitation. If you receive this error statement, navigate to the Microsoft Remote Connectivity Analyzer and perform the DANE validation test against the domain that generated the 4/5.4.312 error. The results show if it's a DNSSEC issue or a different DNS issue. [Section titled: Troubleshooting 4/5.7.321 starttls-not-supported](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#troubleshooting-457321-starttls-not-supported-1) ### Troubleshooting 4/5.7.321 starttls-not-supported Note These steps are for email administrators troubleshooting receiving email from Exchange Online by using SMTP DANE. This error usually indicates an issue with the destination mail server. The Remote Connectivity Analyzer tests connecting with the mail server. Two scenarios generally generate this code: 1. The destination mail server doesn't support secure communication at all, and plain, non-encrypted communication must be used. 2. The destination server is configured improperly and ignores the STARTTLS command. After receiving the message: 1. Check the email address. 2. Locate the IP address that's associated with the error statement so you can identify the mail server the statement is associated with. 3. Check your mail server's setting to make sure it's configured to listen for SMTP traffic (commonly ports 25 and 587). 4. Wait a few minutes, then retry the test with the Remote Connectivity Analyzer tool. 5. If it still fails, try removing the TLSA record and run the test with the Remote Connectivity Analyzer tool again. 6. If there are no failures, this message might indicate the mail server you're using to receive mail doesn't support STARTTLS. You might need to upgrade to one that supports STARTTLS to use DANE. [Section titled: Troubleshooting 4/5.7.322 certificate-expired](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#troubleshooting-457322-certificate-expired-1) ### Troubleshooting 4/5.7.322 certificate-expired Note These steps are for email administrators troubleshooting receiving email from Exchange Online by using SMTP DANE. The sending email server must present a valid X.509 certificate that isn't expired. X.509 certificates must be renewed after their expiration, commonly annually. After receiving the message: 1. Check the IP address that's associated with the error statement, so you can identify the mail server it's associated with. Locate the expired certificate on the email server you identified. 2. Sign in to your certificate provider's website. 3. Select the expired certificate and follow the instructions to renew and pay for the renewal. 4. After your provider verifies the purchase, download a new certificate. 5. Install the renewed certificate into its associated mail server. 6. Update the mail server's associated TLSA record with the new certificate's data. 7. After waiting an appropriate amount of time, retry the test with the Remote Connectivity Analyzer tool. [Section titled: Troubleshooting 4/5.7.323 tlsa-invalid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#troubleshooting-457323-tlsa-invalid-1) ### Troubleshooting 4/5.7.323 tlsa-invalid Note These steps are for email administrators troubleshooting receiving email from Exchange Online by using SMTP DANE. This error code relates to a TLSA record misconfiguration. The error code can only be generated after a DNSSEC-authentic TLSA record is returned. However, many scenarios during the DANE validation occur after the record is returned that can result in the code being generated. Microsoft is actively working on the scenarios that this error code covers, so that each scenario has a specific code. Currently, one or more of these scenarios can cause the generation of the error code: 1. Authentic TLSA record is misconfigured. 2. The certificate isn't yet time valid or is configured for a future time window. 3. Destination domain is under attack. 4. Any other DANE failure. After receiving the message: 1. Check the IP address that's associated with the error statement to identify the mail server. 2. Identify the TLSA record that's associated with the mail server. 3. Verify the configuration of the TLSA record to ensure that it signals the sender to perform the preferred DANE checks and that the correct certificate data is included in the TLSA record. 1. If you need to update the record for discrepancies, wait a few minutes, then rerun the test with the Remote Connectivity Analyzer tool. 4. Locate the certificate on the mail server. 5. Check the time window for which the certificate is valid. If it's set to start validity at a future date, it needs to be renewed for the current date. 1. Sign in to your certificate provider's website. 2. Select the expired certificate and follow the instructions to renew and pay for the renewal. 3. After your provider verifies the purchase, you can download a new certificate. 4. Install the renewed certificate into its associated mail server. [Section titled: Troubleshooting 4/5.7.324 dnssec-invalid](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#troubleshooting-457324-dnssec-invalid-1) ### Troubleshooting 4/5.7.324 dnssec-invalid Note These steps are for email administrators troubleshooting receiving email from Exchange Online by using SMTP DANE. Exchange Online generates this error code when the destination domain indicates its DNSSEC-authentic but Exchange Online can't verify it as DNSSEC-authentic. This section isn't comprehensive for troubleshooting DNSSEC issues and focuses on scenarios where domains previously passed DNSSEC authentication but don't now. Note Exchange Online also generates this error code if it receives a SERVFAIL response from a DNS server on a TLSA query for the destination domain. After receiving the message: 1. If you're using a DNS provider, such as GoDaddy, alert your DNS provider of the error so they can work on the troubleshooting and configuration change. 2. If you're managing your own DNSSEC infrastructure, many DNSSEC misconfigurations can generate this error message. Check for these common problems if your zone previously passed DNSSEC authentication: 1. Broken trust chain, when the parent zone holds a set of DS records that point to something that doesn't exist in the child zone. Such pointers by DS records can result in the child zone being marked as bogus by validating resolvers. - Resolve by reviewing the child domain's RRSIG key IDs and ensuring that they match with the key IDs in the DS records published in the parent zone. 2. RRSIG resource record for the domain isn't time valid, it has either expired or its validity period hasn't begun. - Resolve by generating new signatures for the domain by using valid timespans. When you send an outbound email, if the receiving domain has DNSSEC enabled, Exchange Online queries for TLSA records associated with MX entries in the domain. If no TLSA record is published, the response to the TLSA lookup must be NOERROR (no records of requested type for this domain) or NXDOMAIN (there's no such domain). DNSSEC requires this response if no TLSA record is published; otherwise, Exchange Online interprets the lack of response as a SERVFAIL error. As per [RFC 7672](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7672), a SERVFAIL response is untrustworthy; so, the destination domain fails DNSSEC validation. Exchange Online defers this email with the following error: `450 4.7.324 dnssec-invalid: Destination domain returned invalid DNSSEC records` [Section titled: If the email sender reports receipt of the message](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#if-the-email-sender-reports-receipt-of-the-message) ### If the email sender reports receipt of the message If you're using a DNS provider, such as GoDaddy, alert your DNS provider of the error so that they can troubleshoot the DNS response. If you're managing your own DNSSEC infrastructure, the issue could be with the DNS server itself or with the network. [Section titled: Frequently Asked Questions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#frequently-asked-questions) ## Frequently Asked Questions [Section titled: As an Exchange Online customer, can I opt out of using DNSSEC and DANE?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#as-an-exchange-online-customer-can-i-opt-out-of-using-dnssec-and-dane) ### As an Exchange Online customer, can I opt out of using DNSSEC and DANE? We strongly believe DNSSEC and DANE significantly increase the security of our service and benefit all of our customers. Over the last year, we worked diligently to reduce the risk and severity of the potential impact this deployment might have for Microsoft 365 customers. We actively monitor and track the deployment to ensure negative impact is minimized as it rolls out. Because of this, tenant-level exceptions or opt-out isn't available. If you experience any issues related to the enablement of DNSSEC and DANE, the different methods for investigating failures noted in this document help you identify the source of the error. In most cases, the issue is with the external destination party and you need to communicate to these business partners that they need to correctly configure DNSSEC and DANE in order to receive email from Exchange Online using these standards. [Section titled: How does DNSSEC relate to DANE?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#how-does-dnssec-relate-to-dane) ### How does DNSSEC relate to DANE? DNSSEC adds a layer of trust into DNS resolution by applying the public key infrastructure to ensure the records returned in response to a DNS query are authentic. DANE ensures that the receiving mail server is the legitimate and expected mail server for the authentic MX record. [Section titled: What is the difference between MTA-STS and DANE for SMTP?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#what-is-the-difference-between-mta-sts-and-dane-for-smtp) ### What is the difference between MTA-STS and DANE for SMTP? DANE and MTA-STS serve the same purpose, but DANE requires DNSSEC for DNS authentication while MTA-STS relies on certificate authorities. [Section titled: Why isn't Opportunistic TLS sufficient?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#why-isnt-opportunistic-tls-sufficient) ### Why isn't Opportunistic TLS sufficient? Opportunistic TLS encrypts communication between two endpoints if both agree to support it. However, even if TLS encrypts the transmission, a domain can be spoofed during DNS resolution such that it points to a malicious actor's endpoint instead of the real endpoint for the domain. This spoof is a gap in email security that MTA-STS and SMTP DANE with DNSSEC address. [Section titled: Why isn't DNSSEC sufficient?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/security-and-compliance/how-dane-secures-email#why-isnt-dnssec-sufficient) ### Why isn't DNSSEC sufficient? DNSSEC isn't fully resistant to man-in-the-middle attacks and downgrade (from TLS to clear text) attacks for mail flow scenarios. The addition of MTA-STS and DANE along with DNSSEC provides a comprehensive security method to thwart both MITM and downgrade attacks.
